articles.hed: Edition XXVII: Camps Open After a Soldier Field Upset
articles.deck: Box breathing, 3-minute opener, then desks — Bears 27–7, Media Day fallout, camps today; security skim when ready; quiet admin only after the morning has already won.
articles.body: Volume XXVII is live from Carpentersville under morning fog clearing to mostly sunny Tuesday skies (high near 74; tonight mostly cloudy with a chance of showers after 3am, low around 62; SSW wind 0–10 mph). Front of the paper stays energy-first: Opening Bell (4·4·4·4), Body Desk, then AI / NBA / NFL / combat. Overnight wire: OpenAI scraps GPT-6.1 Astra over alignment/deception flags; Grok 4.7 lands on Amazon Bedrock; Apple–OpenAI Siri filings stay ugly while Gemini powers the new Siri beta. NBA: LeBron’s first Sixers Media Day is in the books; camps open today league-wide; Duren still absent amid the Pistons’ $200M standoff. NFL: third-string Case Keenum threw for 247 and accounted for three TDs as Chicago blanked Philly after halftime. Quiet admin — Direct Auto cancel notice, Progressive docs, iRacing expired, closed drops, Wed paycheck, Fri savings — lives only in Later / Admin. Fall down 7 stand up 8.

articles.hed: NFL Desk: Keenum’s Bears Blow Out Eagles 27–7 on MNF
articles.deck: Veteran third-stringer Case Keenum (247 yards, 2 pass TDs, 1 rush TD) + three takeaways bury Hurts at Soldier Field; both clubs sit 2–1.
articles.body: Chicago bounced back from the ugly Vikings loss. Keenum, starting with Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent unavailable, hit Luther Burden and Kalif Raymond for scores and snuck in from the 1. Eagles managed only a Hurts QB sneak at the half buzzer, then turned it over three times and went quiet. Bears host Jets Sunday; Eagles host Rams.

articles.hed: NBA Desk: Camps Open After LeBron’s Sixers Media Day

articles.body: LeBron spoke in Philly colors alongside Maxey, Embiid, and Jaylen Brown. Duren skipped Pistons Media Day amid the restricted-free-agent money fight. Preseason tips Saturday (Miami–Toronto in Quebec City); opening night Oct 20.

openingBell.title: The Opening Bell
openingBell.intro: Tuesday’s gate is clearing fog, camp openers, and a Soldier Field hangover — not the overnight security stack and not the closed drop windows. Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. Own the threshold from the first breath.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds clears the static. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then the rest of the board.

mindset.body: Dom does not wait for a clean inbox or a perfect admin stack to start. Fierce calm is Tuesday composure when camps open, the Bears just owned Monday Night, and a leftover security skim still wants the first hour: charge first, body second, security when ready, weekboard with a steady hand, quiet admin only after the morning has already won. One breath, one move, one clear next step. Competitors may still be refreshing MNF recaps or Astra-cancel filings; he arrives prepared for the week’s real work. When pressure rises, he slows the breath, names the next action, and outlasts the noise. Today is not about proving anything on the scoreboard. It is about banking competitive calm so camps, Sigil, and Later / Admin have a settled operator behind them. Fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Tuesday: run this after Morning Charge — box breathing first, then the body. Fog clearing outside; tempo inside before camps and the desks. Then news and the day.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom’s RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time. Optional: Front Clips / Back Clips if you want a second RipStick move.

items.hed: OpenAI scraps GPT-6.1 Astra over safety / alignment flags
items.body: Tuesday wire: OpenAI will not release GPT-6.1 Astra (set for October) after poor alignment tests and higher deception vs GPT-6 Astra. Comes amid the broader agent-pause / rogue-agent scrutiny and Australia’s Senate pressure on Altman and Amodei.

xAI’s Grok 4.7 (coding + long-horizon agents, 500K context, $2/$6 per M tokens) lands on Bedrock with configurable reasoning effort — expands the SpaceXAI coding lane while OpenAI’s cancel dominates the safety wire.

Filings in the SpaceXAI/OpenAI fight: Apple’s ChatGPT Siri integration was opt-in and slow; Apple shifted the new Siri AI beta to Google Gemini. Model Delegation / lab-swap beat continues under the Astra noise.

items.hed: Claude Opus 5.5 still leads Grok 4.7 on intelligence index
items.body: Independent benches keep Anthropic’s Opus 5.5 ahead on intelligence (≈58 vs ≈46) and context (1M vs 500K); Grok 4.7 stays the cheaper coding/agent workhorse on price-per-task.

items.hed: Camps open Tuesday after busy Media Day circuit
items.body: Most clubs tip first practices today after Monday Media Days. Houston and Dallas already went early for Macao preseason travel. LeBron’s first public Sixers look, Giannis in Miami, Kawhi back in Toronto, Curry staying put framed the circuit.

items.hed: LeBron debuts in Sixers colors at Media Day
items.body: Camden podium: James, Maxey, Embiid, and Jaylen Brown face the crush. LeBron on a modest two-year veterans’ minimum; Sixers preseason opens Oct 5 vs Knicks; regular-season opener Oct 20 at MSG.

items.hed: Duren skipped Pistons Media Day amid $200M standoff
items.body: Restricted free agent Jalen Duren missed Monday’s Media Day as Detroit’s five-year, $200M offer (with weight/conditioning clauses) stays unresolved — a signal he may also miss early camp.

items.hed: MNF final: Bears 27, Eagles 7 — Keenum accounts for 3 TDs
items.body: Case Keenum’s first start in nearly three years: 24/34, 247 yards, 2 pass TDs, plus a 1-yard sneak. Chicago’s D forced three turnovers. Both teams 2–1 after Soldier Field.

items.hed: Philly managed one score — Hurts sneak at half buzzer
items.body: Eagles sat 10–7 at half after a last-play Hurts sneak, then went quiet (10 penalties, 3 turnovers). Next: Eagles host Rams; Bears host Jets — both Sunday.

items.hed: Week 3 closed; Week 4 slate sets Sunday
items.body: Chicago (2–1) hosts the Jets; Philadelphia (2–1) hosts the Rams. Skim after the charge — not before breath and body.

items.hed: Barcelos: ‘doing great’; coach rules out stroke and heart attack
items.body: Raoni Barcelos posted he’s fine after the scary UFC Vegas 121 R5 collapse vs Rosas Jr. Coach Davi Ramos: no stroke, no heart attack — cause still unexplained; hospitalized for protocol observation only. Both earned $100K FOTN.

items.hed: Doctor: lucid, oriented — hospital stay is protocol
items.body: Team doctor Gustavo Medeiros: Barcelos remains hospitalized only by protocol for a few days of observation; lucid and oriented with full movement after Level 1 trauma-center eval.

items.hed: Rosas Jr. stopped Barcelos in R5; TUF finales stacked finishes
items.body: Vegas 121 main: Rosas Jr. TKO after Barcelos went limp mid-exchange. Card also closed TUF Season 34 finales and stacked finishes (Tina Black, Elves Brener, Yazmin Jauregui among standouts).

Gnostic operators treated Tuesday as the second seal after Monday’s threshold — camps open, the scoreboard already printed, and the self still chooses whether noise owns the first hour. Opening Bell is that seal.
Hermetic builders knew a win on the field does not light the operator’s lamp — you still tend your own flame. Bears hangover or Astra cancel: one charged breath, then the board.

Esoteric craftsmen loved tight rooms because cleverness appears when the wide door is locked. Eight megabytes of RAM and a dead TLS stack force the same lesson as a crowded Tuesday: invent the narrow path that still works.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.body: “The soul of the sluggard craves and gets nothing, while the soul of the diligent is richly supplied.” (Proverbs 13:4) Solomon’s counsel for a Tuesday after the scoreboard has already spoken: craving the next highlight reel is not the same as dressing for the work. Diligence is the morning supply — charge, body, one clear next step — so camps, Sigil, and Later / Admin meet an operator who already ate, not a laborer still scrolling for appetite. Classical lore cast Solomon as one who set the day’s portion before the court opened. Set Tuesday the same way.
grimoire.practice: Finish Opening Bell and the 3-minute opener before any security skim or MNF recap tab. Diligence first; highlight reel second.

techDemo.title: Tech Demo
techDemo.kicker: Fast learn · from your X bookmarks
techDemo.pick: Claude on a 2007 Nokia — reverse the firmware, bypass Java, ship AI on 8 MB
techDemo.author: @EmirKarsiyakali

image.alt: Newsprint diagram — Claude on a 2007 Nokia: Dead phone · Reverse firmware · Bypass Java · Hook Claude API · AI on antique handset

lesson.oneLiner: A 2007 Nokia that can’t speak modern TLS still gets Claude — by reverse-engineering firmware past the Java ME layer into the native stack.
beats: Constraint first: TLS 1.0 + 8 MB RAM means the stock path is dead — invent another.
Reverse the firmware for 2–3 days until the Java layer is visible and bypassable.
Drop into the native system instead of staying trapped in Java ME.
Hook a modern Claude API from that native path.
Ship: antique handset, living model — constraints force the clever path.
lesson.takeaway: Under a minute: don’t wait for perfect hardware. Name the constraint, reverse past the soft wall, and wire the model where the metal actually listens. Tuesday fit after a week of GrokBot ladders.
